reflects_period: 2025-2026 rules (no dated instances; rules are stable across years)
basis: US Code 5 USC 6103 (federal holidays), NIST/US DOT daylight-saving rules (Uniform Time Act as amended 2005), typical K-12 and college academic calendars from state/district and university catalogs as recalled, BLS National Compensation Survey for paid-holiday prevalence, FLSA and FMCSA hours rules.

fields.rule.type: fixed (month/day) | nth_weekday (month, weekday, n; n=-1 is last) | relative (offset_days from another holiday) | relative_to_easter | computed | lunar | window | rule | irregular | weekday_in_window.
fields.federal_holidays[].observed_if_weekend: Federal observance rule for fixed-date holidays.
fields.private_sector_paid_day_off: widely (about three-quarters or more of private-sector workers), some (roughly a third to half), few (roughly a fifth); approximate BLS NCS-style prevalence.

start.effect: clocks jump to 03:00 (spring forward, lose an hour)

end.effect: clocks fall back to 01:00 (gain an hour)

exceptions: Arizona (except the Navajo Nation) does not observe DST
Territories (Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, Northern Marianas) do not observe DST
daylight_saving_time.note: Offsets listed are standard time; during DST add +1 hour except Phoenix and Honolulu. Congress has not enacted permanent DST (as of the basis date).

daylight_hours_geometric.note: Geometric day length (sunrise to sunset, no atmospheric refraction; add about 8-10 minutes in practice) by latitude at the solstices and equinox. Use for seasonal light cycles.

instructional_days.note: Most states require 175-180 days; some set hours instead of days.

breaks.name: Thanksgiving break
breaks.when: Wednesday before Thanksgiving through the Friday after (a full week in some Southern districts)

breaks.name: Presidents' Day or mid-winter break
breaks.when: third Monday of February; a full week in the Northeast

breaks.name: Spring break
breaks.when: one week between early March and mid-April (often near Easter)

k12.note: School year start/end shown as windows; the engine should pick a consistent date per region.

spring.classes_begin_window: Jan 12-Jan 25 (often the week of MLK Day)

quarter_system.note: Used by a minority of colleges (e.g. several UC and Pacific Northwest schools).

work.overtime: FLSA: 1.5x regular rate for hours over 40 per week for non-exempt employees; some states add daily overtime (California over 8 h).

paid_time_off_typical.note: BLS NCS style averages for private-industry workers with access; many service workers have none.

work.meal_break: 30-60 min unpaid for shifts over 6 hours in many states

work_shift_patterns.name: Standard office day
work_shift_patterns.notes: Typical salaried or hourly office work; flextime and hybrid/remote variants common. 30-60 min unpaid meal inside the shift.

work_shift_patterns.name: Trades and construction day
work_shift_patterns.notes: Starts 06:00-07:30, ends 15:00-16:00; overtime and Saturdays common in busy season; weather-dependent in construction.

work_shift_patterns.name: Retail rotating shifts
work_shift_patterns.description: 4-8 h shifts, 4-6 days a week, schedule posted 1-2 weeks ahead
work_shift_patterns.notes: Opening, mid and closing shifts; weekends and holiday rushes included; hours vary week to week.

work_shift_patterns.name: Restaurant and counter service
work_shift_patterns.description: Lunch and dinner shifts, 4-6 per week
work_shift_patterns.notes: Weekend and holiday heavy; closing shifts end 22:00-02:00; part-time common.

work_shift_patterns.name: Bar and nightlife
work_shift_patterns.notes: Shift runs about 17:00-02:00; Thursday-Saturday are peak.

work_shift_patterns.name: Three 12-hour shifts
work_shift_patterns.description: 3 x 12 h per week, day or night, rotating weekends
work_shift_patterns.notes: Hospital style: 07:00-19:30 days or 19:00-07:30 nights; 36 paid hours; extra shifts are overtime or per-diem.

work_shift_patterns.name: Four 10-hour shifts
work_shift_patterns.notes: Compressed week, usually Mon-Thu or Tue-Fri; common in pharmacy, manufacturing, warehouses and some trades.

work_shift_patterns.name: Three 8-hour shifts, rotating
work_shift_patterns.notes: 24/7 services; rotation or seniority bidding decides who works nights and weekends.

work_shift_patterns.name: 24 hours on, 48 hours off
work_shift_patterns.description: One 24 h shift (08:00-08:00) then 48 h off (about 2.33 shifts per week on average)
work_shift_patterns.notes: Average about 56 scheduled hours a week; sleep allowed between calls. Some departments use 48/96.

work_shift_patterns.name: School-year day
work_shift_patterns.notes: Summer, winter and spring breaks off (see school_year); pay is often spread across 12 months. Extra duties and grading outside hours.

work_shift_patterns.name: Faculty teaching load
work_shift_patterns.description: Teaching blocks Mon/Wed/Fri or Tue/Thu plus office hours and research
work_shift_patterns.notes: About 9-12 contact hours a week plus preparation and service; paid on a 9-month or 12-month basis; summers lighter.

work_shift_patterns.name: Over-the-road trucking
work_shift_patterns.description: Weeks on the road, days at home
work_shift_patterns.notes: FMCSA hours-of-service: 11 h driving inside a 14 h window, 10 h off duty, 60/70 h cap over 7/8 days, 34 h restart. Paid per mile; typically 2-3 weeks out then 3-4 days home.

work_shift_patterns.name: Local delivery route
work_shift_patterns.notes: Regional or last-mile courier: load-out at the depot, route stops, return; peaks in Nov-Dec.

work_shift_patterns.name: Warehouse and fulfillment shifts
work_shift_patterns.notes: Mandatory overtime during peaks; night shift differential 5-15%.

work_shift_patterns.name: Postal carrier route
work_shift_patterns.description: 6 days a week, rotating day off
work_shift_patterns.notes: Casual 8-10 h days, Saturdays included; parcels push hours up in December.

work_shift_patterns.name: Physician clinic plus call
work_shift_patterns.notes: Clinic 07:30-17:30 with charting after; call weekends or nights; hospital-based doctors use 3x12 or similar.

work_shift_patterns.name: Evening cleaning crew
work_shift_patterns.notes: Commercial buildings cleaned after hours (18:00-02:00).

work_shift_patterns.name: Security 12-hour shifts
work_shift_patterns.notes: Posts are staffed 24/7; overtime common.

work_shift_patterns.name: Salon and personal services by appointment
work_shift_patterns.notes: Saturdays busiest; Sunday/Monday often closed; booth rent or commission common.

work_shift_patterns.name: Childcare center day
work_shift_patterns.notes: Center open about 06:30-18:00; staff work staggered open/close shifts.

work_shift_patterns.name: Gig and app work, self-scheduled
work_shift_patterns.notes: Demand peaks 07:00-09:30 and 16:00-19:00 on weekdays and Friday/Saturday 17:00-02:00; no guaranteed hours.

work_shift_patterns.name: Student part-time
work_shift_patterns.notes: Federal Work-Study / campus jobs cap at about 20 h a week in term; evenings and weekends.

work_shift_patterns.name: Summer full-time job
work_shift_patterns.description: Mon-Fri or retail schedule for 8-12 weeks
work_shift_patterns.notes: June-August seasonal work: camps, lifeguards, retail, landscaping.

work_shift_patterns.name: Seasonal outdoor work
work_shift_patterns.notes: Fewer paid weeks in cold climates; included in weeks_per_year.
